summary: The paper investigates modular model stitching by transplanting a feed-forward module from Qwen2.5-Coder-7B into block 27 of Qwen2.5-14B with trained block 28 adapters. The benchmark methodically documents a negative transfer result on Python delimiter repair, demonstrating that intact donor capabilities failed to carry over despite extensive control comparisons.
strengths: Rigorous experimental design incorporating essential negative controls, including native host, zeroed output, affine map only, intact general donor, and shuffled donor controls.
Precise architectural specification and hyperparameter disclosure, including the exact 275,268,608 parameter count for the trainable Qwen2.5-14B transformer block.
Sound statistical reporting with paired 95% bootstrap confidence intervals for contrasts between experimental arms.
Honest discussion of negative results and counterintuitive findings, such as the shuffled control outperforming the intact graft.
weaknesses: Evaluated on a very narrow synthetic delimiter repair task with a tiny training budget (16 examples, 8 Adam updates), leaving generalizability to broader coding tasks unverified.
The anomaly where the shuffled module solved 13 complete groups compared to 0 for the intact graft is noted but remains unexplained without multiple seed runs.
Lacks an officially attached repository bundle in the submission metadata, relying instead on inline text URLs.
suggestions: Conduct multi-seed trials across different training data subsets to establish variance bounds for the shuffled control anomaly.
Test grafting across multiple alternative layer depths (early, middle, and late blocks) rather than a single fixed splice site.
Evaluate transfer on standard coding benchmarks (e.g., HumanEval or MBPP sub-tasks) in addition to synthetic delimiter repair.

claims.text: Bansal and colleagues used learned connections between segments of trained networks to test whether their representations were compatible.
Only the 275,268,608 parameters of block 28 receive task gradients.

novelty_vs_existing.title: Revisiting Model Stitching to Compare Neural Representations
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: Applies model stitching principles specifically to isolated feed-forward module transplantation across differing model sizes (7B specialist to 14B host) with selective layer retraining on LLM code generation tasks.
